summary_paragraph: A 31-year-old woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia, chronic tracheostomy, asthma, and GERD was admitted for worsening shortness of breath, thick green tracheal secretions, and dizziness. She had been on ciprofloxacin and prednisone without improvement. Evaluation revealed leukocytosis and orthostatic hypotension. A bronchoscopy cleared obstructive secretions, leading to symptom improvement. A chest CT showed ground-glass opacities concerning for infection, though sputum cultures were negative, suggesting resolving inflammation. Her tachycardia was linked to albuterol use and resolved with medication adjustment. Dizziness resolved with IV fluid rehydration. The omeprazole dose was increased for GERD prophylaxis. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged for laryngeal stenosis and a thyroid nodule noted on imaging.
problems: Other diseases of trachea and bronchus
